bridges.domain: reachable kernel control, checked finite identities, complete service access and dynamic handle typing
assumptions: Control events represent scheduler custody at launch, retained cleanup, explicit resume and finish. Host task ownership and the source-to-control-event mapping remain explicit runtime contracts; no conclusion is supplied as a step premise.

checkedNext uses a natural limit. UINT64_MAX instantiates service/revision capacity; actual checked_add calls reject exhaustion before the modeled registry writes. Revision restart failure is tested through the real Fiber API.

An exhausted service notification revision permanently removes that implementation from candidate resolution. Captured snapshots are revalidated against absence; a freshly provided implementation obtains a fresh UID.

The complete get_value body and Scoped::from_binding are copied unchanged into the compiled probe. Stable arenas, scope owner correspondence and lookups supply valid records. Any downcast and Arc pointer identity use the Rust standard library.

get_value error categories preserve optional/required/unauthorized distinctions. Metadata declaration lookup uses requester; outer-to-inner intercepts use caller. Declaration metadata of another dynamic type defaults; a matching interception of another type triggers the existing production panic. User-defined Merge code, middleware behavior and error location/display formatting remain environment behavior.

Finite notification-count addition still uses the USize capacity premise in KernelRefinement. Arena generation reuse, allocation failure, compiler, language memory safety and host scheduling are part of the trusted runtime boundary.
